Please Note:

CapiSign only PDF files to be e-signed. 

When signing from a smartphone, please use the landscape mode.

Help/Guide

Navigation: Capisign > Sign Documents > Sign & Send > Upload Document

Following navigation process, a user is able to upload a document into Capisign module to get it signed by client. 

Once performed, a user is able to select a file from the list and upload it into the system as shown above.

Once processed, a user is required to click the “Next button” to upload a document.

Once performed, a user is required to add signatories to perform the upload.

Once it has been done, a user is able to drag across relevant tags, add or delete signatories and review the document.

Once performed, a user is able to add a message to Signatories, set reminders and send a document to a client.

		To sign a document received by email.

Help/Guide

Navigation: Email

Once an accountant sent a request to sign the required document, a user is able to perform a signing process directly from the email inbox by clicking the “Review & Sign” button. 

Once it has been done, a user will be redirected to a portal to perform a signing process. It could be done by double-clicking to the relevant “Signature” area and adding the user’s signature.

Once performed, a user is able to finalise a process by agreeing to the “Terms of Service” and clicking on the “Approve and Send” button.

Once approved and sent, a user will be notified with the disclaimer “Signed Successfully!”.

Once an accountant sent a request to sign essential documents, a user is able to perform a signing process directly from email inbox by clicking the “Review & Sign” button.

Once it has been done, a user will be redirected to a portal to perform a signing process. It could be done by double clicking to the relevant “Signature” area and adding user’s signature. Once approved and sent, a user will be notified with the disclaimer “Signed Successfully!”. 

To sign another document, a user should click the “Review & Sign” button on the same email and repeat the signing process for the selected document. 

Once performed, a user is able to finalise a process by agreeing to the “Terms of Service” and clicking to the “Approve and Send” button.

Once approved and sent, a user will be notified with the disclaimer “Signed Successfully!”. 

At the end of the process, a user and a client will be notified about the result of the signing process via email.

### Complete Overview of Capisign

			Print

	Modified on: Tue, 5 Nov, 2024 at 10:31 PM

CapiSign Updates – 5th November 2024

We’re thrilled to share some exciting updates to CapiSign, designed with your feedback in mind! Our latest release includes several key features to enhance your experience and streamline your workflow.

Here's what's new:

New Settings Interface: We’ve revamped the settings to give organisations more control over the visibility of documents, making it easier to align with your internal processes. Now you can manage document access with greater precision and flexibility.

Email Templates: You asked, and we listened! CapiSign now offers the ability to create and send custom email templates. This means you can personalise your communications, making your e-signing process even more professional and tailored to your needs.

Custom Logos: We've made it even easier for you to add your personal touch to your documents. You can now customise your logos with more options, helping your brand stand out in every signed document.

Enhanced E-Sign Details: For better tracking and security, we’ve improved the e-signature capture. The last page now displays additional details such as the IP address and the exact date the document was signed. Plus, a clear note will be added after each signature, confirming that the document has been electronically signed.

Other Articles for Further Guidance

Setting Up CapiSign

Before you begin using CapiSign for electronic signatures, it’s important to configure your settings to align with your practice's requirements. For a detailed explanation of how to set up CapiSign in Capium, check out our Settings Guide for CapiSign. This guide covers key areas like visibility, organisational customisation, and 2FA when sending documents.

Setting Up Your Signature in CapiSign

Creating a personalised signature is one of the first tasks in CapiSign. Learn how to upload your handwritten signature or create a digital version using the platform in our guide on My Signature: Uploading Your Sign.

Creating Email Templates in CapiSign

CapiSign allows you to automate your email workflow by creating and managing email templates. Learn more about how to create, edit, and send documents with personalised templates in our article on Templates in CapiSign.

Sending Documents for E-Signature

Once your signature templates are set up, you can easily apply them across multiple documents. Find out how to add your signature and send documents for e-signature in our guide on Sending Documents for E-Signature.

Managing Drafts: Archiving and Deleting

Not ready to send a document yet? Learn how to save documents as drafts, access them later, and manage your draft workflow efficiently in our guide on Archiving Drafts and Deleting Drafts. This feature helps keep your workspace organised when managing multiple signing requests.

### Capisign: Sending a file from Accounts Production to get e-signing

			Print

	Modified on: Mon, 20 Mar, 2023 at  9:35 AM

		To send a file from Accounts Production to Capisign you can click on this link. Alternatively you can also follow the navigation as shown below.

Navigation: Accounts Production > Client Specific > Annual Accounts

Step 1 - Once you are in Accounts Production, select the specific client 

Step 2 - Select the ‘Reports’ dropdown, and select ‘Annual Accounts’

Step 3 - You will see a list of already generated Annual Accounts, select the ‘Action’ dropdown and then select ‘Send to Capisign’

Step 4 - You will then be taken to the Capisign module where you can view the document and receive an email update. The client will receive an email link to e sign the document and the Capisign status will change to 'Signed' once they have completed the e-signing

### Delete Draft Document from Capisign

			Print

	Modified on: Thu, 23 Oct, 2025 at  9:20 AM

		We understand that you may need to delete draft documents from time to time, and we're here to help you with that. Follow the steps below to remove draft documents from CapiSign:

1. Navigate to CapiSign and check the box for the document you want to remove. Then, click on "Archive" (refer to the attachment for visual guidance).

2. After completing step 1, go to the Archived section in CapiSign, check the box for the document, and click on "Delete" (refer to the attachment for visual guidance).

3. Once you have completed the above steps, navigate to the respective module, select the specific client, click on "Action," and then click on "Send to CapiSign."

By following these steps, you will be able to successfully delete draft documents from CapiSign. If you have any further questions or need additional assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out to our customer support team.

We understand that you may need to delete draft documents from time to time, and we're here to help you with that. Follow the steps below to remove draft documents from CapiSign:


1. Navigate to CapiSign and check the box for the document you want to remove. Then, click on "Archive" (refer to the attachment for visual guidance).


2. After completing step 1, go to the Archived section in CapiSign, check the box for the document, and click on "Delete" (refer to the attachment for visual guidance).


3. Once you have completed the above steps, navigate to the respective module, select the specific client, click on "Action," and then click on "Send to CapiSign."


By following these steps, you will be able to successfully delete draft documents from CapiSign. If you have any further questions or need additional assistance, please don't hesitate to reach out to our customer support team.
